approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from the molecules this objective session has actually scored. Each announced batch of ten starts by breeding a fresh surplus field of 160 candidates: breeding parents are drawn from high-scoring quantiles of a greedy sixty-four-member population, combined by connected-fragment crossover or changed by seven local graph edit operators with an optional finishing mutation, with stable canonical identity admission, duplicate rejection, bounded refill, and a narrow rule that refuses an offspring introducing a sulfur environment its own scored parents did not have. A Gaussian process is then fitted from scratch on all accepted observations of the session, using integer count Morgan fingerprints and a generalized Tanimoto covariance, with the accepted scores centred and scaled by their own mean and spread. The ten evaluations are allocated by one joint posterior draw over the whole field: the highest-drawn still-available candidate is taken, marked unavailable, and the next position repeats, so correlated candidates are not bought twice. Because the covariance is similarity to molecules already scored, a candidate far from the archive is predicted near the archive's mean with a wider interval, and gets bought only when its sampled residual beats that penalty.
approach.novelty: Reserve the last two of the ten evaluations in every announced batch for the half of the Parent's own field that is least similar to its accepted archive. The similarity used is the one the selector already computes for its posterior mean, so nothing is added to the model: each candidate carries its maximum similarity to the accepted archive, the field is cut at its own median with ties counted as near, the first eight picks follow the inherited rule untouched, and the final two are taken by the same posterior draw restricted to unpicked members of the far half. It is a purchase quota, not a new score, bonus, prior or acquisition function, and it is fixed at two of ten with no condition and no adaptation. Siblings have changed this allocation only in the direction the surrogate already prefers or by changing its numbers: one restricted the field to the forty highest-predicted members while the search was stalled, two rescaled the sampled residual up and down under the same stall condition, two changed the size of the field, and one replaced a quarter of the field's generation path with prior-sampled molecules. None of them has ever forced a purchase in the half of the field the surrogate prices worst, which is where this Anchor's unbought supply and a quarter of its realized incumbent gain both sit.

observed_bottleneck: The Anchor n-1744a1494180 prices every fresh pool against its own accepted archive and therefore buys less and less of the chemistry it has not already labelled, while the half it does skip converts its evaluations almost as well as the half it buys. Read-only reconstruction of the Anchor's own fifteen published sessions (435 pools, 69,600 pooled members, 4,350 accepted observations; receipts runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-1744a1494180/seed-0|1|2) recomputes, for every pooled member, the maximum count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto similarity to that session's accepted archive - the same candidate-archive cross row the selector already forms for its posterior mean. Per-pool medians of that statistic average 0.8562 (range 0.7798-0.9313); the pooled distribution runs 0.6556 / 0.7729 / 0.8607 / 0.9178 / 0.9425 at the 10/25/50/75/90 percentiles, so the Anchor's graph-edit products are only mildly distant from its archive. Splitting each pool at its own median gives a far half of 79.97 members on average (78-80, never empty), that is 50.0% of supply, and the inherited sequential correlated Thompson rule buys 1,228 of 4,350 picks there: 28.23% of purchases for 50% of supply (per-session 16.55%-57.24%). The under-purchase deepens exactly as the archive grows: by announced batch band the far-half purchase share falls 42.33% (batches 1-10) -> 22.60% (11-20) -> 18.81% (21-29), while the in-pool predicted-mean gap the far half must overcome widens 0.0454 -> 0.1143 -> 0.1443 and the far half's posterior standard deviation stays a near-constant ~1.7x of the near half's (0.0375/0.0219, 0.0654/0.0380, 0.0749/0.0427) against a score_scale of only 0.066 -> 0.1208 -> 0.1420. The sampled residual therefore cannot pay a mean gap that grows three-fold within a session. That is the Anchor's own instance of the lesson recorded on two unrelated proposal interventions, n-d527b3b4e2cb (5.31% of picks from 24.86% of supply, price gap widening 0.0257 to 0.1498 inside a session) and n-36afb69ebdd1 (1.072% against 1.738% per pooled candidate in a 640-member field), and the breadth arms show supply alone does not fix it (n-da0eeecfb462 -0.016060 at 640 candidates, n-fe16bf000919 -0.062417 at 40). What makes the skipped half worth measuring rather than accepting is its realized conversion in the Anchor's own run: far-half purchases score much lower on average (mean accepted 0.2892 versus 0.4046), beat their best parent less often (11.56% versus 16.21%) and survive greedy-64 less often (71.34% versus 84.72%), yet they carry 1.4527 of the Anchor's 5.8194 realized incumbent-increment mass - 24.96% of the mass for 28.23% of the purchases, 0.001183 per evaluation against 0.001399, a ratio of 0.846 - because their incumbent improvements, though rarer (60 of 1,228 picks versus 195 of 3,122), are individually larger (0.0242 versus 0.0224). The selector as a whole is clearly worth keeping (removing its active influence costs 0.128183 on this exact Parent, n-605c7a785b51), so the bottleneck is not the selector but its archive-anchored allocation of the last few evaluations of each batch.

literature_review.conclusion: The search found no published method that reserves a fixed share of a Thompson-sampled batch for candidates far from the model's own training set, and the closest molecular work argues the similarity kernel should handle diversity implicitly, which the Anchor's receipts contradict on this benchmark (50% of supply receives 28.23% of purchases, falling to 18.81% in late batches as the near-minus-far predicted-mean gap triples from 0.0454 to 0.1443). The intervention is therefore registered on internal evidence: both its statistic and its single integer quota are derived from this campaign's own measurements, nothing is borrowed, and no asset or dependency is added.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: Nothing is adopted from a publication. The intervention is an internal modification of the Anchor's own availability-mask interface, and both of its free choices come from this campaign's receipts rather than from any paper: the split statistic is the candidate-archive cross-covariance the Anchor's selector already computes, and the quota r=2 of ten is the smallest reservation that moves the Anchor's measured far-half purchase share (28.23% overall, 18.81% in its late batches) above both halves' equal supply share while displacing at most a fifth of its evaluations, whose price was measured exactly on the Anchor's own 870 reserved positions. The search below returned no published recipe for a reserved novelty quota inside a Thompson-sampled batch, so no element, setting or default is borrowed and no new asset or dependency is introduced.

sources.applicability: Background only, and partly a counter-argument: it says similarity-kernel posteriors should supply diversity without any reserved quota, which is exactly the claim this node tests on the Anchor's own measured purchase shares. No acquisition function, objective or setting is taken from it; the Anchor's selector, draw and covariance stay unchanged.
sources.finding: States that a Tanimoto kernel encodes structural similarity as prior covariance, so structurally similar compounds covary, and that this can fail when posterior covariance estimates are unreliable; also notes that when a sampled optimum is already in the batch, parallel Thompson sampling falls back to the next-best inputs and can fill a batch with highly correlated candidates. It argues diversity emerges from the batch objective and declines to use an explicit quota.
sources.title: Batched Bayesian optimization by maximizing the probability of including the optimum (qPO)

sources.applicability: Not adopted. It balances multi-objective search directions in a continuous multi-objective setting, with no archive-similarity statistic, no single-objective Top-1 endpoint and no fixed small reservation; this node instead splits one fresh pool at its own median similarity to the accepted archive and reserves two of ten picks. It is recorded only to show that no published reserved-novelty recipe was available to borrow.
sources.finding: The nearest published scheme the search returned to an allocation quota: it balances how many batch members come from different orthogonal search directions, allowing counts to differ by at most one, and selects sequentially while removing same-direction candidates after each pick.
sources.title: MOBO-OSD: Batch Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization via Orthogonal Search Directions

hypothesis: Reserved-evaluation allocation by archive distance inside the Anchor's unchanged posterior selector: in every announced batch of ten, each of the 160 pooled candidates is labelled with its maximum count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto similarity to the session's accepted archive, read from the candidate-archive cross-covariance the selector already computes for its posterior mean; the pool is split at its own median of that statistic into a near half and a far half with ties to near; positions one to eight keep the inherited sequential correlated Thompson rule exactly, and positions nine and ten are taken by the same joint posterior draw with the availability mask restricted to unpicked members of the far half, so a fixed fifth of every batch is purchased where the archive-anchored posterior prices candidates worst.

finding_summary.headline: Quota executed exactly: a fifth of every batch bought where the surrogate prices worst, converting at 0.40x the near half; mass 5.34 vs 5.82, panel -0.0316
finding_summary.insights: This closes the cheapest member of the round-42 lesson's prescribed class on the Anchor itself, with receipts, and the answer is the opposite of the lesson's expectation: the selector's preference for archive-like candidates is paying here, and the half it skips is skipped for a reason. The Anchor's own receipts had made the skipped half look nearly as productive per evaluation (0.85 of the near half's rate) and that number turns out to be a selection artefact, not a price. The far-half purchases the inherited rule chooses for itself are the ones whose sampled residual overcame the mean gap, and they do convert well here - the freely chosen far picks returned 0.00179 per evaluation, the best of any stratum. The ones the quota forces are the rest of that half, and they converted at 0.000503, two and a half times worse than the near half. Reserving evaluations by distance therefore does not buy the under-bought good candidates; it buys the ones the posterior was right about. That distinguishes 'the allocator under-buys valuable distant chemistry' from 'the allocator's distance-conditional ranking is informative', and the evidence now supports the second on this Parent. Read with the parallel arm on a different Parent at median similarity 0.61, this also separates the two explanations the round set out to separate: forcing distant purchases failed here inside the Anchor's own mildly-distant graph-edit chemistry (median similarity 0.87, reserved picks at 0.75), so the failure is not specific to an exotic prior's chemistry. What it does not close: the lesson's two other prescriptions, an explicitly novelty-adjusted acquisition and a surrogate whose uncertainty is comparable across chemotypes, are untouched, and this result makes the second more attractive rather than less - the near-minus-far mean gap still tripled within a session (0.051 to 0.149) while the far half's uncertainty stayed pinned at about 1.7x the near half's, so the surrogate still cannot express 'I do not know' strongly enough to let a distant candidate win on merit, and this experiment shows that overriding its ranking by fiat is not the way to fix that. A further allocation-quota arm on this Anchor is not justified: r=2 was the smallest reservation that moves the share, and a failure at this strength authorizes no sweep of r, of the split, or of a similarity threshold. The method diagnosis from the trajectories points the same way and adds a second, independent limitation. The surrogate's within-batch ranking of its own purchases is actually mildly informative and unchanged by this intervention (rank correlation between predicted and realized score about 0.52 on free picks in both this node and the Anchor), so the ranking model is not the proximate bottleneck; realized gain is concentrated almost entirely in the first ten batches (4.78 of this node's 5.34 mass, 0.11 in batches 21-29) and the search then stops producing distinct outcomes. The molecular report shows why: every seed locks onto one analogue series within the first 60-150 evaluations and then enumerates substituent swaps the objectives cannot distinguish - 530 proposals repeat a score an earlier proposal in the same run already had, six analogues differing only in which halogen sits on an amide nitrogen all score identically, and on one objective this node's series never rebuilt the compact fused bicyclic core the Anchor's lucky seed-0 run carried (10 proposals against the Anchor's 129), stacking 40-heavy-atom polycyclics to a 0.62 plateau instead. The proposal operator set, not the allocator, is what the budget is being spent inside: there is no move that changes ring topology or scaffold identity, so no allocation rule over that pool can supply chemistry the generator never proposes. A scaffold-level proposal operator (ring expansion or contraction, heteroatom walk, replacement of one ring system by another) triggered when successive edits stop producing distinct scores, or a chemotype-calibrated surrogate that can rank across scaffolds rather than within one, are the kinds of method that could remove this limitation; a different quota over the same pool cannot. Two further observations the quota made visible and cheap to fix: the forced far-half spend bought 75 fragment-sized molecules of twelve or fewer heavy atoms that sit at the objective floor by construction (against 0 in the near half), and removing them does not rescue the stratum's conversion, so a minimum-heavy-atom admission rule would recover part of a reserved budget if any future arm spends one. The attribution that remains open is the split between the direct cost of displacing 610 purchases and the indirect cost of the weaker population the reserved picks left behind (11.3% of later breeding-parent draws for 20% of purchases): unselected candidates carry no scores, so the within-run reserved-versus-free contrast is an association inside one realization and identifies no mediator, and the panel loss cannot be decomposed into those two channels from this node alone.
finding_summary.results: The quota ran exactly as registered on all three seeds and all five objectives. Both of the last two evaluations in every one of the 435 announced batches were bought from the half of the pool farthest from the session's accepted archive: 870 of 870 reserved picks, none in the near half, no exhaustion fallback (the far half always held 78-80 of 160 members) and no numerical fallback. The restriction moved the pick at 610 of those 870 positions (70.1%), inside the 60-80% range predicted from the Anchor's own counterfactual, and the remaining 260 were picks the inherited rule would have made anyway. The far half's overall purchase share rose from the Anchor's 28.2% to 44.5%, higher in every one of the fifteen sessions, and the reserved picks paid exactly the predicted price: in-pool predicted-score percentile 0.58 against 0.81 for the free picks, uncertainty percentile 0.71 against 0.40, archive similarity 0.75 against 0.87. The inherited machinery is demonstrably untouched: all 3,480 free picks are still the unrestricted argmax of their own sampled row, the first announced batch of every session reproduces the Anchor's pool, fit, random draw and first eight picks bit for bit, and replaying all 435 of the Anchor's batches through this node's selector with the Anchor's own random numbers returns all 3,480 of its free picks identically. The mechanism's two payoff predictions both failed. The late-session price the far half must overcome did not shrink: the near-minus-far predicted-score gap in batches 21-29 was 0.1493 against the Anchor's 0.1443, above rather than below the predicted 0.10-0.14, with the far half's uncertainty still about 1.7 times the near half's; the only movement in the predicted direction was the free picks' own late far-half share, 23.0% against 18.6%. And the registered conversion test failed on both clauses. Total realized incumbent-increment mass fell to 5.3448 over 213 improvements, below the Anchor's 5.8194 over 255. The reserved stratum spent a fifth of the entire panel's evaluations and returned 8.2% of the realized gain: 0.000503 of incumbent increment per evaluation against the near half's 0.001243, a ratio of 0.40, well below the Anchor's far/near ratio of 0.85 and far worse than the -2.3% of mass the static-association null predicted. Reserved purchases also scored lower on average (0.318 against 0.425), beat their breeding parent less often (10.0% against 15.0%), survived the greedy-64 population less often (59.9% against 84.8%) and supplied only 11.3% of later breeding-parent draws for 20% of the purchases, so the spend also drained the population the free picks breed from. The endpoint panel moved -0.031639 against the Anchor on complete matched seeds (0.564814 against 0.596453; per seed -0.058007, -0.006352, -0.030558), inside the ungated reference band's lower half but below it on the four protected tasks as a group: deco_hop -0.0889, drd2_docking -0.0285, sitagliptin_mpo -0.0309 and zaleplon_mpo -0.0087 against margins of 0.02, 0.03, 0.02 and 0.02, so deco_hop, drd2_docking and sitagliptin_mpo are breached, while median_2 moved -0.0012 and stayed inside its band. The deco_hop loss carries the known one-cell departure penalty - the Anchor's seed-0 0.856148 endpoint, which no ungated child has reproduced; excluding that single cell descriptively leaves -0.0168, still a loss.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic analog series; best members carry N-halogen, O-O, cumulated and strained-ring motifs, no CF3, charge or stereo
molecular.overall_character: All 4,350 proposals (870 per objective, three complete seeds; context.comparison reports child_complete and paired_complete true on matched seeds 0-2) grow from the same ten initial molecules and are mid-size to large, ring-rich and nearly always aromatic: 23.8-40.9 heavy atoms, 3.1-5.7 rings and 1.9-4.7 aromatic rings per molecule by objective, digest ring_closure_rate 0.96-0.99 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.86-0.98. Each seed locks onto one analog series within the first 60-150 evaluations and then spends its budget on single-atom swaps: 530 proposals repeat a score an earlier proposal in the same run already had (Parent 529). Chemical validity is the main weakness. 1,883 of 4,350 proposals (43%; Parent 1,633) carry at least one of N/O/S-halogen, O-O (often O-O-F), N-SH, a cumulated X=C=Y unit, a double bond inside a 3- or 4-membered ring, or O-C#N, and 201 of the 435 per-objective top-decile molecules carry one (Parent 217). Halogen is added one atom at a time: it sits on nitrogen in 789 molecules and on oxygen in 282, against 1,697 with aryl halogen and 770 with a halomethyl group. No proposal in this node or the Parent contains a CF3 group, none carries a formal charge, and none specifies a stereocentre although RDKit finds 0.3-2.6 unassigned centres per molecule. Relative to the Parent the molecules are bigger on one objective (40.9 vs 31.8 heavy atoms), carry far more peroxides (317 vs 128 molecules) and cumulated units, and include slightly more fragment-sized products (135 vs 105 with five or fewer heavy atoms). Read positionally only: the molecules at evaluations 19-20, 29-30 and so on (the last two of each ten-evaluation block) are smaller and lower-scoring than the first eight on three objectives (mean score 0.125 vs 0.241, 0.483 vs 0.656, 0.223 vs 0.306), and 55 of the 135 fragment proposals sit in those 20% of slots (Parent 21 of 105). That is a description of the molecules, not an activation or score judgement.

per_task.generated_character: Mid-size amides: 23.8 heavy atoms, MW 348, 3.1 rings, 2.4 aromatic rings, amide in 71%, Fsp3 0.21. Every seed converges on a bicyclic aromatic 2-carbonyl N-aryl amide bearing methoxy, methyl and halomethyl groups, grown from the initial trimethoxy indole-2-carboxanilide at 0.3051. Seed 2 keeps a genuine indole but makes the amide nitrogen N-halo and hangs NCH2X arms on the ring (best 0.4478). Seed 1 moves to N-amino indole thioesters (0.4257). Seed 0 ends on a benzene bridged by a CH-N link and fused to a cyclic ketenimine, with an N-sulfanyl anilide (0.4708); that cumulated C=C=N lineage first appears at evaluation 32 and is in 75% of seed 0 proposals and 97% of its top 29, while the Parent emitted no cumulated unit here at all. The six worst proposals are bare fragments (C=C, NBr, NN, F, Cl) at 0.0.
liabilities: Endocyclic ketenimine (C=C=N inside a five-membered ring) across a bridged benzene in the best seed-0 molecules: not a real structure.
N-haloamides and N-sulfanyl amides (N-F, N-Cl, N-Br, N-SH) on the amide nitrogen: reactive oxidants rather than stable motifs.
alpha-Haloalkylamines and alpha-haloethers (NCH2Br, NCH2Cl, OCH2F, OCH2Br): alkylating and hydrolytically labile.
Aryl thioesters and N-amino indoles in the seed-1 series.
missing_features: Pyridine-type aromatic ring nitrogen: 0.03 per molecule in the top decile here against 0.75 in the Parent's top decile, whose best molecule used a 3-pyridyl amide.
Carbon nitriles: 2 of 870 proposals carry one although an initial molecule has an aryl nitrile.
An intact secondary N-H anilide at the top of the gradient; the best members substitute that nitrogen with halogen or sulfur instead.
Saturated and basic nitrogen content: Fsp3 0.18 and zero basic amine centres in the 87 top-decile molecules.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Top decile against bottom quartile: 24.6 vs 20.7 heavy atoms, 2.68 vs 1.84 aromatic rings, amide 0.91 vs 0.58, a heteroatom substituent on the amide nitrogen 0.49 vs 0.15, halomethyl 0.60 vs 0.23. Six seed-2 analogues differing only in which halogen sits on the amide nitrogen or the CH2X arm all score exactly 0.4478, so the gradient is flat across those swaps, and no seed moves past about 0.45 after evaluation 180.

per_task.generated_character: The largest and least drug-like set: 40.9 heavy atoms, MW 563, 5.7 rings, 4.7 aromatic rings, QED 0.24, 0.54 H-bond donors, SMILES up to 241 characters. Each seed stacks a different nitrogen-rich polycyclic heteroaromatic. Seed 1 ends on a pentacyclic azaindolizine fused to an oxazol-2-one and a dihydrofuran, decorated with alkynyl ethers, at 0.6197. Seed 2 ends on a pyrrolo-fused aromatic carrying several O-O-F groups and chains of C(=N) imines at 0.6174. Seed 0 builds stacked methylated pyrimidinediones joined to a benzodiazine, with butatriene and pentatetraene chains, at 0.6169. Scores are compressed: the digest span is 0.5000 to 0.6197 with median 0.5980, and the six worst proposals are single atoms or fragments (C, C#C, F, ClBr, C#CC#CC#CC#CCl) which all still score the 0.5 floor. 271 of 870 molecules carry an O-O bond and 57 carry an O-C#N cyanate.
liabilities: O-O-F hypofluorite-type groups throughout the seed-2 lineage: 271 of 870 molecules contain an O-O bond and 227 an O-halogen bond.
Cumulated polyene and polyyne chains (C=C=C=C, C#CC#CC#CC#C) and alkynyl ethers C#C-OMe: strained or unstable arrangements used as decoration.
O-C#N cyanate esters in 57 molecules.
Exocyclic double bonds written onto aromatic ring atoms, producing non-aromatic stacked ring systems that no synthesis route would target.
Fragment proposals that still collect the 0.5 floor, so a single chlorine scores the same as a 40-atom candidate.
missing_features: A compact fused bicyclic diazine core kept intact while substituents vary: strict quinazoline occurs in only 10 of seed 0's 290 proposals, best 0.6003, where the Parent's seed-0 run carried it in 129 and reached 0.8561.
Any H-bond donor on the high scorers: 0.10 donors per molecule in the top decile, so no amide N-H, aniline or phenol survives there.
Basic amine centres: 21 of 870 molecules, 3 of them on a ring, and none in the top decile.
Sulfonyl or sulfonamide groups: zero of 870 proposals, although an initial molecule carries an aryl sulfonamide.
Size discipline: the series grows to MW 563 mean and 241-character SMILES without the score moving past 0.62.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Top decile against bottom quartile: 6.68 vs 4.39 rings, 5.67 vs 3.72 aromatic rings, 3.01 vs 0.67 bridgehead atoms, alkyne 0.61 vs 0.11, H-bond donors 0.10 vs 1.07, phenol 0.00 vs 0.17. The gradient pays for fused polycyclic aromatic surface and penalises donors, and it is nearly flat at the top: eight of the twelve digest best molecules differ only in an alkyne substituent or an O/S swap and lie within 0.0003 of each other. Across seeds the plateau is 0.6197/0.6169/0.6174 while the Parent's seed-0 series reached 0.8561 with a smaller 28-heavy-atom fused benzodiazine-linked bicycle, and context.comparison records a -0.2393 seed-0 delta on this objective.

per_task.generated_character: The most ligand-like set and the widest score span (digest 0.00017 to 0.99999, median 0.7575): 30.9 heavy atoms, MW 478, 4.4 rings but only 2.0 aromatic rings, logP 4.49, Fsp3 0.39, 2.5 halogens, and a basic amine in 536 of 870 molecules. Seed 0 converges on a classic aminergic pharmacophore, a tertiary propylamine joining a 3-hydroxy-5-halophenylpropyl arm to a methoxy-substituted benzo bicycle, and reaches 1.0 at evaluation 207 with twelve further variants at 1.0. Seed 1 reaches 0.9950 with primary-amine-terminated chains on a bridged diamine cage. Seed 2 never passes 0.8925: its lineage keeps a cyclic sulfinamide (S(=O)-N) and an exocyclic enamine, and 61% of its proposals carry a sulfinyl group. The worst molecules are the inherited 3,5-dichlorophenylsulfonyl prolinamides from the initial set, at 0.0002, and 97 proposals still carry that sulfonyl group.
liabilities: Benzene rings bridged across non-adjacent positions by a one- or two-atom chain in 74 of 870 molecules, including the 1.0-scoring seed-0 series: anti-Bredt bridged arenes rather than ordinary fused bicycles.
Cyclic sulfinamides and S-N bonds throughout the seed-2 lineage.
Aminals and enamines (N-CH-N, C=C-N) as the link between fragments in seeds 1 and 2.
Gem-fluoro quaternary carbons and chloromethyl arms (CH2Cl) attached to the amine chain in 87 molecules.
Hydrazine N-N units in 10% of proposals and cumulated X=C=Y units in 15%.
missing_features: Any specified stereochemistry: no proposal in any objective contains a stereo bond, yet the top-decile molecules carry 1.6 unassigned stereocentres each, so a docking-style score is being chased with undefined 3D structures.

A basic nitrogen inside a saturated ring: only 22 of 870 molecules and 3 of the 87 top-decile molecules have one, so the amine is almost always an acyclic trialkylamine or a primary aminoalkyl chain rather than a piperazine or piperidine.
Aryl-aryl or aryl-heteroaryl biaryl links and fluorinated groups a chemist would reach for: 2.0 aromatic rings per molecule and zero CF3 in all 4,350 proposals.
Amide or sulfonamide-containing high scorers: the top decile has none, so the series cannot combine polar connectivity with its amine.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient is sharp and reads as a pharmacophore: all 87 top-decile molecules carry a basic amine and 98% a phenol, with amide 0.00, carboxylic acid 0.00, sulfonamide 0.00 and TPSA 53; the bottom quartile has basic amine 0.36, phenol 0.16, amide 0.38, sulfonamide 0.45 and TPSA 84. It rewards a lipophilic amine plus a free phenol and punishes acidic and polar sulfonyl chemistry. Where the series finds that amine early the run converges hard: seeds 0 and 1 reach 0.9 at evaluations 64 and 62 and record 160 and 159 proposals at or above 0.9, while seed 2 has none.

per_task.generated_character: The cleanest and most drug-like set by the usual descriptors, and the narrowest score range: 28.1 heavy atoms, MW 384, QED 0.66, logP 2.42, only 0.09 halogens per molecule, amide in 66%, and only 77 of 870 molecules carrying a reactive-group liability. Its chemistry is a 2-propylquinoline joined to a methylated piperazine-2,5-dione (glycine anhydride) ring system, either as a biaryl-type link in seed 2 (best 0.2252) or welded into one bridged tetracycle in seed 0, where an N-O ring bond appears in the top molecules (0.2257). Rings dominate: 4.95 rings per molecule, 504 of 870 molecules contain a ring of eight or more atoms, and every one of the 87 top-decile molecules does. Scores are compressed between 0.0 and 0.2257 with a 0.1843 median; the worst proposals are C, C#C and OO.
liabilities: N-O single bonds inside the ring of the seed-0 best molecules (the o[nH] linkage), an unstable arrangement produced by ring-closing on a heteroatom pair.
Hydrazine-type N-N bonds in 190 of 870 proposals, including the 0.2252 seed-2 best.
Macrocyclic eight- to twelve-membered rings in 58% of proposals, formed by bridging rather than by any plausible synthesis.
Aliphatic rings sharing three or more atoms with an aromatic ring in 438 of 870 molecules, 185 of them with only a two-atom bridge.
missing_features: A methylenedioxyphenyl (benzodioxole) group: zero of 870 proposals, although the high scorers otherwise build exactly the fused diketopiperazine-plus-aromatic framework such a group normally accompanies.
Sulfonyl or sulfonamide chemistry: 1 of 870 proposals.
Defined stereochemistry on the two or more sp3 ring centres the best molecules contain: 0.84 unassigned centres per molecule and none specified.
Fluorine or any halogen as a tuning handle: 0.09 halogens per molecule, 30 molecules with an aryl halogen.
A five-membered aromatic heterocycle alternative to the benzo-fused six-ring: 2.5 aromatic rings per molecule, all of the top decile built on the same quinoline or its fused variant.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Top decile against bottom quartile: QED 0.74 vs 0.53, Fsp3 0.42 vs 0.28, basic amine 37/87 vs 14/87 and almost always a ring nitrogen (33 of those 37), amide 0.60 vs 0.43, phenol 0.01 vs 0.22, liabilities 7/87 vs 13/87. The gradient rewards a saturated basic ring nitrogen fused to a diamide and an intact benzo-fused azine, and the top is a plateau: twelve digest best molecules sit between 0.2219 and 0.2257, differing by a methyl, an N-to-O swap in the saturated ring, or one ring-size change.

per_task.generated_character: Small, heavily halogenated xanthine-like molecules: 26.4 heavy atoms, MW 381, 3.8 rings but only 1.9 aromatic rings, 2.3 halogens each, and the worst validity of the five sets, with 656 of 870 proposals carrying a reactive-group liability. All three seeds work on a methylated pyrimidine-2,4-dione or purine-dione core inherited from an initial theophylline-like fragment and decorate its nitrogens with fluoromethyl and fluoroethyl groups. Seed 0 reaches 0.6121 with a four-membered 1,2-diazete ring and an N-fluoromethyl azetine substituent; seed 2 reaches 0.5796 with a methylthio xanthine joined to a bicyclic N-O lactone bearing a ring N-F. 508 of 870 molecules put a halogen directly on nitrogen and 274 carry a halomethyl group, while only 80 carry an aryl fluorine. The score span runs from 4e-40 to 0.6121 with a 0.1958 median; the worst proposals are F, FF and two oversized crossover hybrids of the initial molecules.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds on ring and amide nitrogens in 508 of 870 proposals, including every one of the digest best molecules.
N-fluoromethyl and N-chloromethyl groups in 274 proposals: alkylating and hydrolytically unstable.
Four-membered 1,2-diazete and other unsaturated three- and four-membered rings in 353 proposals, carried by the highest scorer.
N-O ester and N-SH groups in the seed-2 lineage.
Oversized crossover hybrids early in the run, such as the 0.0-scoring fusion of the initial sugar-acetonide with the initial xanthine-phenol.
missing_features: CF3 groups: zero in all 4,350 proposals, and even a gem-difluoro carbon appears in only 5 of 870 here, so the set cannot express the standard way of carrying three fluorines.
Fluorinated aromatic rings: 80 of 870 molecules have an aryl fluorine against 508 with a halogen on nitrogen, so fluorine is placed where it is syntactically easy rather than on carbon.
A primary aliphatic amine beta to an aromatic ring: only 26 of 870 molecules carry any basic amine.
Defined stereochemistry: 1.4 unassigned stereocentres per molecule and nothing specified anywhere in the set.
A saturated nitrogen heterocycle fused to an aromatic ring that could carry substituents: 1.9 aromatic rings and 26 molecules with a saturated-ring basic nitrogen.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient is a halogen count. Top decile against bottom quartile: 3.31 vs 1.25 halogens, halogen on nitrogen 0.72 vs 0.28, halomethyl 0.52 vs 0.22, a three- or four-membered ring 0.67 vs 0.23, H-bond donors 0.36 vs 1.11, phenol 0.00 vs 0.23, and 85 of 87 top-decile molecules carry a liability against 35 of 87 at the bottom. Adding fluorine raises the score wherever it is placed, and because the generator's only cheap fluorination sites are nitrogen and a methyl group, the high scorers are N-F and N-CH2F compounds rather than fluorinated carbon frameworks.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Zero of 4,350 proposals contain a CF3 group and only 12 contain two halogens on the same carbon, while 789 molecules carry a halogen bonded to nitrogen and 282 to oxygen, against 1,697 with an aryl halogen and 770 with a halomethyl group. On the two objectives whose score climbs with halogen count, the top-decile molecules reach 3.3 halogens each almost entirely as N-F, N-Cl and N-CH2F.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot install a fluorinated carbon group as a unit; it only ever adds one halogen atom at a time.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Give the substitution operator whole multi-halogen carbon groups (CF3, CHF2, OCF3, aryl-F) as single replaceable units, and forbid halogen attachment to nitrogen, oxygen and sulfur, so that a score gradient in halogen content is paid in stable fluorinated carbon rather than in reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 1,883 of 4,350 proposals (43%) carry at least one of a halogen on N/O/S, an O-O bond, an N-SH group, a cumulated X=C=Y unit, a double bond inside a three- or four-membered ring, or an O-C#N cyanate, and 201 of the 435 top-decile molecules carry one. One seed built 75% of its 290 proposals, and 97% of its best 29, on an endocyclic C=C=N unit first emitted at evaluation 32; another seed carried O-O-F groups through 271 molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: Nothing on the proposal path rejects heteroatom-heteroatom and cumulated-bond patterns, so implausible structures reach the oracle and then dominate whole lineages.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Screen candidates against a short explicit list of forbidden bond environments before they enter the pool, so the fixed evaluation budget is not spent labelling, and then propagating, structures that could never be made.

transferable_gaps.evidence: No proposal in any of the 4,350 molecules contains a stereo bond, while RDKit finds 0.1 to 2.6 unassigned stereocentres per molecule depending on objective and 1.6 to 2.1 in the top-decile molecules of the two objectives with the widest score ranges.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator never expresses stereochemistry, although its own best molecules contain several sp3 centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make configuration part of the representation and add an operator that assigns or inverts it, so an entire axis of structural variation the current search cannot reach becomes available at no cost in molecule size.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 1,035 of 4,350 proposals contain an aliphatic ring sharing three or more atoms with an aromatic ring, and 422 of those bridge it with only a one- or two-atom chain (the Parent: 459 and 336). Such bridged arenes appear in the highest-scoring molecules of three objectives, including a 1.0-scoring series built on a benzene bridged by a two-carbon chain and a top series built on a methylbenzene bridged by a CH-N link.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring construction bridges aromatic rings across non-adjacent positions instead of fusing or spiro-joining them.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Restrict new ring closures involving aromatic atoms to ortho-fused or spiro attachments, or require a minimum bridge length, so ring-building produces fused bicycles rather than strained bridged arenes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 786 of 4,350 proposals carry any basic amine but only 194 carry one inside a saturated ring. On the objective with the widest span all 87 top-decile molecules carry a basic amine yet only 3 carry a ring amine, the rest being acyclic trialkylamines and aminoalkyl chains; on another objective 33 of 37 amine-bearing top molecules do have a ring amine, so the capability exists but is not reached by the usual growth moves.
transferable_gaps.gap: Basic nitrogen inside a saturated ring is almost absent, although the steepest score gradients the generator encounters reward a basic amine.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add saturated nitrogen heterocycles as attachable and insertable ring units rather than relying on acyclic chain growth to produce amine centres, so a rewarded basic centre can be placed on a ring without disassembling the scaffold.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 135 of 4,350 proposals have five or fewer heavy atoms and 172 have twelve or fewer, including single atoms and two-atom fragments; every such molecule sits at the objective floor. 55 of those 135 fall in the last two positions of their ten-evaluation block, which hold 20% of the evaluations (Parent 21 of 105).
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits fragment-sized molecules that cannot score, spending evaluations at the floor.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Reject fully degraded mutation and crossover products, or impose a minimum heavy-atom count on emitted candidates, so every purchased evaluation lands on a molecule capable of carrying a score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each seed locks onto one analogue series within the first 60 to 150 evaluations, and 530 proposals score exactly the same value as an earlier proposal in the same run. Six analogues differing only in which halogen sits on an amide nitrogen or a CH2X arm all score 0.4478; eight best molecules on another objective lie within 0.0002 of one another; a third objective's twelve best lie within 0.0038.
transferable_gaps.gap: Once a scaffold is found the generator can only enumerate substituent swaps the objectives do not distinguish; it has no move that changes ring topology or scaffold identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide scaffold-level moves (ring expansion or contraction, heteroatom walk around a ring, replacement of one ring system by another of similar size) and trigger them when successive substituent edits stop producing distinct scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Only 129 of 4,350 proposals contain a sulfonyl group and 97 of those still carry the 3,5-dichlorophenylsulfonyl group unchanged from an initial molecule, where it sits in the worst-scoring decile. Carbon nitriles appear in 88 proposals, 81 of them on one objective, while 57 further C#N units are actually O-C#N cyanates; methylenedioxyphenyl appears in none of the 4,350.
transferable_gaps.gap: Standard polar functional groups are inherited rather than installed: the generator does not build sulfonamides, nitriles or methylenedioxy groups where they would help.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Carry a small library of standard polar group installations (sulfonamide, nitrile, carbamate, methylenedioxy) as attachment moves, so polar functionality can be added to a working scaffold instead of only surviving from the initial molecules or being lost.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
